questions.question_text: When salt BA is treated with Conc. $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ reddish brown gas is liberated. The aqueous solution of BA gives pale yellow precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ solution. Which of the following anion ( $\text{A}^{-}$ ) is present in the salt BA?
questions.question_html: When salt BA is treated with Conc. $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ reddish brown gas is liberated. The aqueous solution of BA gives pale yellow precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ solution. Which of the following anion ( $\text{A}^{-}$ ) is present in the salt BA?
questions.explanation_text: The anion present is $\text{Br}^{-}$ . When a bromide salt is treated with concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ , reddish brown vapours of bromine are liberated. First, hydrogen bromide is formed: $\text{BBr}+\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4} \rightarrow \text{BHSO}_{4}+\text{HBr}$ Then $\text{HBr}$ reduces concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ and gets oxidised to bromine: $2\text{HBr}+\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4} \rightarrow \text{Br}_{2}+\text{SO}_{2}+2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ The bromine vapours, $\text{Br}_{2}$ , are reddish brown in colour. Also, the aqueous solution of the salt gives a pale yellow precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ solution: $\text{Ag}^{+}+\text{Br}^{-} \rightarrow \text{AgBr}$ Silver bromide, $\text{AgBr}$ , is pale yellow. So, the anion $\text{A}^{-}$ present in the salt $\text{BA}$ is: $\text{Br}^{-}$ Correct option: D.
questions.explanation_html:
The anion present is $\text{Br}^{-}$ .

When a bromide salt is treated with concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ , reddish brown vapours of bromine are liberated.

First, hydrogen bromide is formed:

$\text{BBr}+\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4} \rightarrow \text{BHSO}_{4}+\text{HBr}$

Then $\text{HBr}$ reduces concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ and gets oxidised to bromine:

$2\text{HBr}+\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4} \rightarrow \text{Br}_{2}+\text{SO}_{2}+2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$

The bromine vapours, $\text{Br}_{2}$ , are reddish brown in colour.

Also, the aqueous solution of the salt gives a pale yellow precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ solution:

$\text{Ag}^{+}+\text{Br}^{-} \rightarrow \text{AgBr}$

Silver bromide, $\text{AgBr}$ , is pale yellow.

So, the anion $\text{A}^{-}$ present in the salt $\text{BA}$ is:

$\text{Br}^{-}$

Correct option: D.

options.label: A

options.html: to increase the concentration of $OH^{-}$ ions

options.label: B

options.label: D

questions.explanation_text: In the analysis of III group basic radicals of salts, the purpose of adding $NH_{4}Cl(s)$ to $NH_{4}OH$ is, to suppress the dissociation of $NH_{4}OH$ due to the common ion effect.
